inspection_outcome: Six numbered findings: one Major VEM potential failure and five Minor endpoint, boundary-domain, degree and sign corrections.
summary: Valid lowest-order data make (4.9) nonunique or inconsistent; Theorem31 depends on an invalid perfect-pairing inference. VEM cohomology and DDR algebraic chains are separately supported and not declared false.

problems.title: VEM potential wedge pairing is degenerate and can be inconsistent
problems.claim: Equation (4.9) defines a unique map from all VEM data to P^-_{r+1} Lambda^k; its moments imply polynomial reproduction.
problems.assumptions: Legal r=0, convex regular interval/triangle/cube, centers specified, Cartesian DOFs exactly from (4.1).
problems.check_method: Root reconstructed admissibility, Koszul bases, Hodge signs, wedge pairing and theorem dependency; exact rational integral script independently run.
problems.decisive_evidence: Interval d=1,k=r=0, zero data: P=0 and P=x both solve mean-zero equation. Triangle d=2,k=1,r=0, center(1/3,1/3), alpha=-(y-1/3)dx+(x-1/3)dy, edge DOFs 0, cell alpha,D=0: trial span(dx,dy,alpha) pairs to 0 with alpha, but RHS integral |alpha|^2=1/18. Cube d=3,k=2,r=0 with nu=xdy-ydx gives 0=-16/3. Polynomial beta=(45/8)(1-x^2)(1-y^2)(1-z^2) star nu interpolates to that cube datum.
problems.result: Confirmed nonuniqueness and nonexistence for permitted inputs; not a numerical approximation.
problems.counterevidence: Global differential (4.6) and cohomology Theorem 30 do not use (4.9); extension (4.20) uses DDR(0) potentials. DDR proof chain unaffected by this objection.
problems.impact: VEM potential as a map, Theorem 31's moment-to-polynomial inference and dependent higher-dimensional reconstruction (4.11) need substantial repair.

correction.statement: Redesign a nondegenerate trial/test pairing compatible with desired reproduction and DOFs.
correction.verification: Simple Hodge-dual target would reconstruct only constants on r=0 interval, so cannot reproduce x; no complete replacement certified.

independent_acceptance_check.assumptions_checked: r0, convex shape-regular cells, specified centers; legal independent Cartesian DOFs. Trial and test spaces are the printed trimmed polynomial spaces, not silently Hodge-dual substitutes.
independent_acceptance_check.decisive_evidence: Interval d1,k0, zero data: trialspan{1,x}, testconstant, so0 andx both solve. Triangle d2,k1,centroid(1/3,1/3),alpha=-Ydx+Xdy,zeroedge/derivative data: trialspan{dx,dy,alpha}; each wedge pairing withalpha integrates0. Star^-1alpha=Xdx+Ydy, so Eq4.9 demands0=?(X?+Y?)=1/18. Each centered moment is1/36 from area1/2,?x1/6,?x?1/12.
independent_acceptance_check.smooth_antecedent_and_sign: Cube d3,k2,r0,omega=xdy-ydx gives trialproxy a+b(x,y,z), orthogonal/odd pairing0, while RHS=-16/3. beta=(45/8)(1-x?)(1-y?)(1-z?)star(omega) has zero face traces and projection multiplier(45/8)(128/135)/(16/3)=1; derivativecomponent K0^0=0. Thus even interpolated smooth data fail.
independent_acceptance_check.core_dependency: Eq4.9 map and Theorem31's moment-to-polynomial inference fail; higher-dimensional derivative4.11 depends on this potential.
independent_acceptance_check.counterevidence_and_repair: Global4.6 uses4.4/stored derivatives, and Theorem30 extension4.20 uses DDR(0) potentials, so VEM cohomology is not refuted. A Hodge-dual target alone destroys interval reproduction ofx. No complete alternative construction certified.

problems.title: The k=0 harmonic mode invalidates the unrestricted inf-sup claim
problems.claim: Topologically trivial Omega has trivial harmonic spaces, for k>=0, giving uniqueness and (3.21).
problems.assumptions: Nonempty connected contractible domain, unreduced de Rham complex, natural boundary weak formulation, standard zero negative-degree space.
problems.check_method: Root substituted c_h=I_r^0(1) using polynomial consistency and commutation, checked g=0 and g=1.
problems.decisive_evidence: c_h!=0 and d_r c_h=0; A((0,c_h),(0,v_h))=0 for every test but graph norm positive. g=1 tested by c_h gives 0=(c_h,c_h)>0.
problems.counterevidence: Poincare statement (3.20) itself permits preimage zero for constant input. Theorem 14 correctly preserves H^0=R.
problems.impact: Application's unqualified endpoint solvability and inf-sup range are false.

correction.statement: Restrict application to 1<=k<=n on contractible domain, or impose zero mean, compatible forcing and/or harmonic unknown at k=0.
correction.verification: Directly removes constant kernel and compatibility obstruction; no new full analytic convergence theorem claimed.

independent_acceptance_check.decisive_evidence: On connected contractible domain the unreduced complex has H0=R. c_h=I_r^0(1) is nonzero with d_rc_h=0, so bilinear form annihilates(0,c_h) against every test but its graph norm is positive. For forcing1, testingc_h gives0=positive mass.
independent_acceptance_check.counterevidence_and_repair: Restrict1<=k<=n, or impose zero mean/compatible forcing/harmonic variable. Original3.20 can choose zero preimage forconstantinput; Theorem14 retainsH0 correctly. No cohomology theorem refutation.

problems.title: Adjoint-consistency estimate omits natural boundary conditions
problems.claim: Every sufficiently smooth omega has adjoint defect O(h^{r+1}) under additional piecewise regularity.
problems.assumptions: Omega=(0,1)^3, ell=0, r>=1, regular refining mesh, omega=dx1, mu_h=I_r^0(x1).
problems.check_method: Root used exact commutation and vanishing polynomial stabilization to calculate defect and norm.
problems.decisive_evidence: delta omega=0; d_r mu_h=I_r^1 dx1; defect=-1 and graph norm squared=4/3, independent of h.
problems.result: Confirmed failure of stated universal smooth-form scope.
problems.counterevidence: Actual mixed solution and derivative may satisfy required natural conditions through weak equations. General-dimension proof is explicitly left open, not misrepresented as supplied.
problems.impact: Definition/estimate scope needs boundary domain; restored application not refuted.

correction.statement: Require Hilbert-adjoint domain / homogeneous normal trace tr(star omega)=0 for smooth forms, or retain boundary pairing.
correction.verification: Continuous integration by parts identifies missing term; no complete external estimate independently re-proved.

independent_acceptance_check.assumptions_checked: Cube(0,1)^3,ell0,r>=1,regular refining mesh; omega=dx1 andmu_h=I_r^0x1 are smooth polynomial data.
independent_acceptance_check.decisive_evidence: deltaomega0,d_rmu=I_r^1dx1; polynomial stabilization vanishes. Adjoint defect exactly-1, graph norm?=1/3+1=4/3, so mesh-independentO(h^(r+1)) estimate cannot hold for all smoothforms.
independent_acceptance_check.counterevidence_and_repair: State the Hilbert-adjoint domain/homogeneous normal trace tr(staromega)=0, or retain boundarypairing. Actual weak solution may enforce this domain. General-degree proof explicitly deferred by authors is a limitation, not separately manufactured error.

problems.title: Two-dimensional radial proxy has wrong polynomial degree
problems.assumptions: Paper's Koszul and rotated proxy conventions, including r=0.
problems.check_method: Root applied kappa to P_{r-1} Lambda^2 and checked lowest order.
problems.counterevidence: Formal Koszul, trimmed-space and DDR definitions use correct degree.
problems.impact: Explicit vector proxy and uses of that named space would have extra DOFs if implemented literally.

correction.verification: Follows exactly from (2.5); r=0 then zero.

independent_acceptance_check.decisive_evidence: K_r^1=kappa P_(r-1)??, so rotated radialproxy is(x-xF)P_(r-1). At r0 the formal space iszero but printed(x-xF)P1 is nonzero.
independent_acceptance_check.counterevidence_and_repair: Restore r-1. Formal Koszul/trimmed/DDR definitions already have the correct degree; no invalidation of their algebraic proof.

problems.title: Two-form contraction proxy has reversed cross product
problems.claim: First-slot contraction of two-form with proxy w by v has proxy v cross w.
problems.assumptions: A.1.4 standard orientation and A.6 first-slot convention.
problems.check_method: Root evaluated dx1 wedge dx2 on e1 and basis tests.
problems.decisive_evidence: omega=dx1 wedge dx2 has w=e3; contraction by e1 is dx2 (e2), while e1 cross e3=-e2.
problems.counterevidence: Formal contraction correct; replacing all generators by their negatives preserves Koszul subspace.
problems.impact: Proxy operator translation erroneous, not proof that formal complex fails.

correction.verification: Direct coordinate evaluation and exact vector arithmetic.

independent_acceptance_check.decisive_evidence: First-slot contraction i_(e1)(dx1?dx2)=dx2 withproxye2; printed e1?e3=-e2. Correct proxy isw?v.
independent_acceptance_check.counterevidence_and_repair: Formal contraction is correct and negating all space generators preserves the Koszul span. Correct the translated operator; do not infer failure of the formal complex.

problems.title: Integration-by-parts rewrite has incorrect volume sign
problems.claim: Rewriting (3.4) yields negative integral of d(star^-1 omega_f) plus boundary jump.
problems.check_method: Root algebraically substituted Stokes and independently checked interval r=2 polynomial input x.
problems.decisive_evidence: Correct equation has + integral d a wedge mu. For (0,1),k=0,r=2,data I_2 x,mu=1,boundary jump0, printed equation gives 1=-1.
problems.counterevidence: Original (2.1),(3.4), subsequent complex proof have correct signs.
problems.impact: Explanatory DDR/DDF comparison formula; not a counterexample to d^2=0.

correction.statement: Replace volume minus by plus, retaining boundary difference as printed.
correction.verification: Exact Stokes identity and explicit interval check.

independent_acceptance_check.decisive_evidence: Stokes gives positive?d(star^-1omega_f)?mu plus boundaryjump. For interval(0,1),k0,r2,I_2x,mu1, thejumpiszero and derivative dx integrates1; printed formula gives1=-1.
independent_acceptance_check.counterevidence_and_repair: Replace volume minus byplus. Original2.1/3.4 and d?=0 proof use correctsigns.

clarifications.text: Higher-dimensional reconstruction is defined only to d=n-1 but later used for d=n. Intended upper bound n remains subject to resolving P1.

Hodge-transform of a trimmed space must not be identified with a trimmed space of complementary degree; dimension 4 versus6 at d3,r1 illustrates it. Moment argument can be interpreted in Hodge-transformed space.
Uniform general-degree adjoint-consistency proof explicitly deferred. Not treated as an author-supplied theorem or a defect by itself.
An extraction-based suspicion was withdrawn after source-image inspection: printed K_{r-1} subset K_r is correct.
